newsitem.title: USA: Cargill, WPL form electricity joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Cargill, WPL form electricity joint venture.

text.p: Cargill Inc, the Minneapolis, Minn.-based commodities giant, and WPL Holdings Inc, said Wednesday they have agreed in principle to form an energy trading and marketing company to enter the U.S. power market.

The new venture, to be called Cargill-IEC, will begin trading electricity as soon as they receive a power marketing license from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), the companies said in a joint statement.
WPL, based in Madison, Wisconsin, is the parent of Wisconsin Power and Light Co.
WPL Holdings is currently merging with IES Industries and Interstate Power Co to form Interstate Energy Corp (IEC).
IEC will eventually become Cargill's formal partner in the new venture, the companies said.

"Cargill-IEC initially will offer a wide range of energy trading, marketing and risk management services to wholesale electricity customers, which include municipal utilities, rural electric cooperatives, power aggregators and investor-owned utilities nationwide," the companies said.

The U.S. power market, estimated by Cargill Energy Division to be worth $300 billion to $400 billion annually, is undergoing extensive deregulation, replacing traditional monopolies with open competition among power producers.
David Gabriel, currently vice president and general manager of Northeast Petroleum, a Cargill company, will manage the new Cargill-IEC venture, the statement said.
